simple.meaning: תְּאֵן (tᵉʼên) is a Hebrew object word meaning “the fig (tree or fruit).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 3:7. The surrounding context includes land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּאֵן (H8384) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תְּאֵן (tᵉʼên) / H8384 is traced through Genesis 3:7, Numbers 13:23, Numbers 20:5, Deuteronomy 8:8 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H8384. teenah תְּאֵנָה noun feminine fig-tree , (then) fig (√ dubious; Arabic , Aramaic תֵּינְתָא , ; perhaps Punic תין (see Lzb 385 ; i.e. תְּיֵן Eut, see DHM VOJ i. 26 ), Assyrian tittu, a tree; Lag M i. 58 ff. combines ׳ת (precariously) with √ (III) אנה meet opportunely , with reference to fructifying of fig by another tree, compare Hom Aufsätze u.Abh. i. (1892), 100 ); — absolute ׳ת Judg 9:10 +; suffix תְּאֵנָתוֺ 1Kin 5:5 +, etc.; plural תְּאֵנִים Num 13:23 +; construct תְּאֵנֵי Jer 24:2 ; suffix תְּאֵנֵיכֶם Amos 4:9 ; — 1 fig-tree ( ficus carica Post Flora. 730; Hast. DB, under the word Tr NHB.350 M'Lean-Th-Dyer Ency. Bib., under the word ; compare Löw § 335 ; often + גֶּפֶן ): Judg 9:10-11 , (in allegory), Amos 4:9 ; Hosea 9:10 ; Nahum 3:12 ; 1Kin 5:5 ; 2Kin 18:31 = Isa 36:16 ; Micah 4:4 ; Isa 34:4 ; Prov 27:18 ; ת ׳עֲלֵה Gen 3:7 (J) fig-leaves , ׳הַתּ פַגֶּיהָ חָֽנְטָה Song 2:13 ; collective Num 20:5 (JE), Hosea 2:14 ; Jer 5:17 ; 8:13 ; Deut 8:8 ; Hab 3:17 ; Hag 2:19 ; Zech 3:10 ; Joel 1:7 , 12 ; 2:22 ; Psa 105:33 . 2 fig , always plural: Num 13:23 (JE), Jer 24:1-2 ,(twice in verse); 24:3 (twice in verse); 24:5 , 8 ; 29:17 (all symbolic of Judaeans), 8:13 ( תּ ׳אֵין בַּתְּאֵנָה ), Neh 8:13 ; as medicament, ת ׳דְּבֶלֶת 2Kin 20:7 = Isa 38:21 ; הַבַּכֻּרוֺת תְּאֵנֵי Jer 24:2 the figs of early ripeness (compare Du). תַּאֲנִיָּה see [I. אנה ]. תְּאֻנִים see I. און .

“Yahweh, the God of Israel says: ‘Like these good figs, so I will regard the captives of Judah, whom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans, for good.

“ ‘As the bad figs, which can’t be eaten, they are so bad,’ surely Yahweh says, ‘So I will give up Zedekiah the king of Judah, and his princes, and the remnant of Jerusalem, who remain in this land, and those who dwell in the land of Egypt.
Yahweh of Armies says: “Behold, I will send on them the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and will make them like rotten figs that can’t be eaten, they are so bad.
“Therefore behold, I will allure her,
I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness.
He has laid my vine waste,
The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withered;
Don’t be afraid, you animals of the field;
“I struck you with blight and mildew many times in your gardens and your vineyards;
But they will sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree;
All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
For though the fig tree doesn’t flourish,
Is the seed yet in the barn? Yes, the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree haven’t produced. From today I will bless you.’ ”
In that day,’ says Yahweh of Armies, ‘you will invite every man his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree.’ ”
